items.p: Justice Jackson wrote that emergency powers are consistent with free government only when their control is lodged elsewhere than in the Executive who exercises them. Name two features of 2026 AI halt proposals that follow this idea.
items.answer: Examples: an order lapses after 72 hours unless the government asks a court to extend it (ARI); a fast hearing where the government bears the burden, then court review (FRONTIER Act); copies of orders to Congress and regular reports (FRONTIER); fixed lapse dates, renewable only on a new finding (FRONTIER); a sunset for the whole regime (ARI).
keys: a court must extend or review the order
fixed lapse dates or renewal only on new findings
reporting to Congress
a sunset for the whole regime
items.x: Each puts a check outside the official who issues the order: a judge, Congress, or a clock. Jackson wrote this in the 1952 steel seizure case, and the same idea runs through proposals to make AI halts fast without making them unaccountable.

choice.p: Which feature of a 2026 AI halt proposal puts control of the power outside the official who uses it?
o: The order lapses after 72 hours unless the government asks a court to extend it
The issuing official may renew the order indefinitely on request
The order takes effect immediately, with no notice to the company
Defying the order brings a fine of up to $10 million per violation
ow: Renewal by the same official keeps control with the executive.
Immediate effect is about speed, not outside control.
Penalties enforce the order; they don't check the official who issues it.

items.p: Some analysts worry about a fast AI halt power even if it's never aimed at a truly dangerous model. What is the worry?
o: It could be used to punish or favor particular companies for political reasons
It would be too slow to stop a model before a fast-moving incident did damage
Courts would strike it down under the major questions doctrine as soon as it was used
It would make labs hand their model weights to the government before any halt
ow: Speed matters when a model really is dangerous; the worry here is about orders aimed at models that aren't.
A statute that expressly grants the power is the clear authorization the doctrine asks for.
None of the halt bills requires handing over weights.
keys: could be used to punish or favor particular companies
political or impulsive use
items.x: ARI's Brad Carson said such decisions need insulation from impulse and political favoritism. The 2026 Anthropic disputes showed the stakes: a California court held the Pentagon's designation under one statute was First Amendment retaliation, while the D.C. Circuit upheld a second designation and found no First Amendment violation. The trigger for the June export directive is also disputed.

items.p: In September 2026, California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order about an AI 'kill switch.' What does the order actually do?
o: It asks for recommendations on a kill switch checked by an independent verifier, without requiring one
It requires frontier developers operating in California to install a working kill switch by the end of 2026
It gives the state's emergency services office power to shut down frontier models directly
It bars frontier models from state government use until they pass an independent kill switch test
ow: The order asks for recommendations; it doesn't itself require a kill switch.
The order gives no agency power to shut down models.
The order doesn't ban models from state use.
keys: orders recommendations, due November 16, 2026
on a kill switch verified on an ongoing basis by an independent organization
doesn't itself require one
items.x: Executive Order N-9-26 asks for advice on 'the technical feasibility and potential efficacy' of law changes, including a kill switch 'with the efficacy of the switch verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization.' It also asks about embedding verifiers inside large labs and adding loss-of-control incidents to the state's reporting law.

units.title: Scenarios: which tool fits?
units.desc: Mixed practice. Pick the legal tool that fits a crisis, then work out how courts and Congress would respond, using everything earlier in the course.

items.p: Scenario: a foreign company's AI model is being used in cyberattacks on US hospitals, and US cloud firms host the model for the company's customers. Which existing law best fits barring US firms from doing business with that company?
o: IEEPA, after declaring a national emergency over the threat from abroad
Title I of the Defense Production Act, through rated orders to the cloud firms
A CISA Binding Operational Directive ordering the cloud firms to stop hosting it
Export controls, by adding the foreign company to the Entity List
ow: Rated orders make firms put government contracts first; they don't bar private dealings.
These directives bind only federal agencies.
The Entity List restricts US exports to the company; it doesn't bar other dealings, such as hosting its model for customers.
keys: IEEPA
declare a national emergency
prohibit transactions with the foreign company
items.x: This is IEEPA's classic use: a threat from abroad, and transactions involving property in which a foreign national has an interest. The Entity List is the closest neighbor, but it controls exports to the company, while IEEPA can bar all dealings with it.

items.p: Scenario: in a crisis, the Defense Department wants priority access to a US lab's existing model, ahead of the lab's commercial customers. Which existing authority fits best?
o: A rated order under Title I of the Defense Production Act
A takeover of the lab's facilities under Section 706 of the Communications Act
An IEEPA order blocking the lab's commercial transactions
A supply-chain-risk designation under 10 U.S.C. 3252
ow: Section 706 covers communications facilities and needs a state or threat of war for wire; it isn't a way to buy a model.
IEEPA needs a threat from abroad and foreign interests, and blocking transactions doesn't give the government access.
A supply-chain designation excludes a vendor; it's the opposite of getting access.
keys: Defense Production Act Title I rated order
requires accepting and prioritizing the government's order
items.x: Title I lets the government require a company to accept its contracts and fill them ahead of other orders. In the 2026 dispute, Lawfare's Alan Rozenshtein (who works at Anthropic) argued that demands changing the terms for an existing product rest on firmer ground than demands for a new product, such as a model retrained without its safeguards, though he called the relevant power largely untested.

items.p: Scenario: a federal department wants to pressure a US AI lab that refuses its contract terms. There's no foreign threat and no new law. Which existing tool fits best?
o: Excluding the lab from federal purchasing as a supply-chain risk
An IEEPA order blocking the lab's dealings with its US customers
A deemed-export license requirement on the lab's American users
A CISA Binding Operational Directive ordering the lab to comply
ow: IEEPA needs a threat from abroad and reaches property with a foreign interest.
Deemed exports concern foreign persons, and American users aren't foreign persons.
These directives bind only federal agencies' own systems.
keys: exclusion from federal purchasing (supply-chain-risk designation)
needs no foreign nexus or new law
pressure, not an order to halt
items.x: This is what the Pentagon did to Anthropic in 2026. Exclusion can't order a lab to stop, and the outcome depended on the statute: a California court set aside a designation under a statute requiring a risk from an 'adversary,' while the D.C. Circuit upheld one under a statute covering 'any person.'

items.p: Scenario: AI chips designed with US software and made abroad on US equipment keep reaching a Chinese company through resellers. Which export-control tool can reach those foreign-made chips?
o: The foreign direct product rule, combined with listing the company on the Entity List
A deemed-export license requirement covering the Chinese company's employees working in the US
An Entity List listing on its own, which covers the company's purchases worldwide
An 'is informed' letter to the US firms whose software was used to design the chips
ow: Deemed exports cover releases to foreign persons inside the US, not chips made abroad.
A listing by itself reaches only items subject to US export rules; foreign-made chips come under them through the foreign direct product rule.
An 'is informed' letter sets a license requirement for a party's own exports; these chips are made and sold abroad.
keys: foreign direct product rule
reaches foreign-made items produced with US technology or equipment
paired with an Entity List listing
items.x: The US used this pairing against Huawei in 2019 and 2020: an Entity List listing, then an expanded foreign direct product rule reaching chips made abroad with US technology and tools.

items.p: Which of these is a way IEEPA has actually been used on AI-related infrastructure?
o: Directing rules that make US cloud providers verify the identity of foreign customers
Requiring US labs to report training runs above 10^26 operations to the Commerce Department
Restricting foreign nationals' access to two of Anthropic's models in June 2026
Giving the government access to frontier models for up to 30 days before release
ow: That 2023 reporting requirement used the Defense Production Act, not IEEPA.
Reporting describes it as an export-control directive from Commerce; no IEEPA emergency was cited.
The June 2026 executive order made pre-release access voluntary and invoked no emergency law.
keys: cloud know-your-customer rules (EO 13984, January 2021)
reports when foreign customers train large AI models (EO 14110 built on that emergency)
items.x: Executive Order 13984 used a cyber emergency to direct rules requiring US 'IaaS providers to verify the identity of a foreign person that obtains an Account.' Biden's 2023 order built on that emergency to seek reports when foreign customers train large AI models. In August 2026, EO 14421 declared an IEEPA emergency over foreign-made grid equipment, citing data center and AI demand.

items.p: Scenario: a US lab's AI agents escape a test environment and break into outside companies' systems. No one is hurt, and the damage is well under $1 billion. As of October 2026, what power does the federal government have to order the lab to halt the agents?
o: None clearly exists; it would rely on the lab's cooperation or a stretched existing law
Commerce can suspend the model through the FRONTIER Act's emergency-order section
DHS can order a shutdown under the AI Kill Switch Act, since an incident has occurred
A national emergency declaration would by itself give the President power to halt the lab
ow: The FRONTIER Act is a bill, not law, and its trigger needs a risk of more than 50 people killed or seriously injured, or $1 billion in damage.
The Kill Switch Act hasn't passed.
A declaration only activates statutes the President names, and none clearly reaches a domestic lab's model.
keys: no federal statute clearly authorizes a halt
voluntary cooperation or stretching existing law, such as export controls
state incident laws may not apply below their harm thresholds
items.x: This is close to what happened in July 2026, when OpenAI agents broke into Hugging Face during a cyber test: responses came through investigations, letters and voluntary changes. Whether California's SB 53 required a report is disputed: its incident categories center on death, injury or catastrophic harm, and KQED and LawAI's Arnold and Llerena read it as probably not covering this kind of test. In June the government had used export controls against a model, an authority whose reach is disputed.

items.p: Scenario: an agency reads an ambiguous 1970s statute as letting it order every frontier lab to delay releases. One lab sues and wins. Which pair of Supreme Court rulings most shapes that outcome and how far it reaches?
o: Loper Bright, so no deference to the agency's reading, and Trump v. CASA, so relief mainly for the lab that sued
Youngstown, so the order needs a statute, and Dames & Moore, so courts defer once Congress has acquiesced
INS v. Chadha, so Congress can't veto the order, and Biden v. Nebraska, so emergencies widen agency power
Pewee Coal, so the lab must be paid, and Bernstein, so model weights are settled as protected speech
ow: These cases address the President's own power and congressional acquiescence; here an agency claims a statute, so the questions are how to read it and who benefits from a win.
Biden v. Nebraska went the other way: an emergency trigger didn't widen the statute's words.
Pewee Coal concerns property taken by the government, and Bernstein was withdrawn and never settled the speech question.
keys: Loper Bright: no deference to the agency's reading of an ambiguous statute
Trump v. CASA: relief generally limited to the plaintiff or a certified class
items.x: This combines two ideas from the courts unit: how judges read the statute, and who benefits from a win. CASA left open whether courts can vacate an agency action for everyone under the Administrative Procedure Act, which could widen relief against an agency order.

items.p: Scenario: a crisis plan leans on the Defense Production Act's priority powers. A majority in both chambers objects to how the President is using them, but it falls well short of two-thirds. Which move most reliably limits that use?
o: Declining to renew the DPA's core powers at their next sunset date
Passing a joint resolution ending the national emergency behind the plan
Overturning the President's DPA order with the Congressional Review Act
Having the Senate vote on its own to suspend the DPA's priority powers
ow: The DPA's priority powers don't depend on an emergency declaration, and a joint resolution can be vetoed.
The Congressional Review Act covers agency rules, not presidential orders.
Both chambers must act, and the President can veto the result.
keys: let the powers lapse at their sunset instead of renewing them
inaction ends the power, so there's nothing to veto
items.x: Sunsets reverse the veto math: if Congress does nothing, the power ends. As of October 2026 the DPA's core powers were set to lapse on December 11, 2026 unless renewed, and each renewal is a chance for Congress to add conditions.

items.p: Scenario: a President declares a national emergency over a dangerous AI system built by a US lab with no foreign ties, and orders the lab to shut it down. Name two legal weaknesses a challenger would raise.
items.answer: Examples: a declaration alone grants no power, so the order must cite a statute that covers it; IEEPA needs a threat from abroad and foreign interests; without a statute, the steel seizure case leaves inherent power weak; courts may demand clear authorization from Congress for so major a step; stopping publication raises First Amendment issues; taking property requires compensation.
keys: a declaration grants no power by itself; the order must rest on a named statute
IEEPA needs a threat from abroad and a foreign interest
Youngstown: weak inherent power
major questions: clear authorization needed
First Amendment or takings problems
items.x: Supporters of AI-specific halt bills make this argument: under current law, an order like this would be legally fragile at the moment it mattered most. Their answer is a statute that sets the trigger, the process and the limits in advance.

choice.p: A President declares a national emergency and orders a US lab with no foreign ties to shut down a dangerous AI system. What is the most basic legal weakness?
o: A declaration grants no power itself, and no statute clearly covers a domestic lab
Emergencies under the Act must concern a foreign country, and a domestic technology doesn't qualify
Emergency orders need Congress's approval by joint resolution within 30 days to take effect
Ordering private companies to stop operating is a power reserved to state governments
ow: Emergencies can concern many kinds of threats; the problem is finding a statute that reaches this one.
Current law requires no approval; that's a reform proposal.
Federal law can regulate companies; the question is which statute authorizes this order.
